title: Saffron Shrikhand with Cardamom Pears
tagline: Silky saffron yoghurt, soft spiced pears, and a pistachio crunch. Very festive.
steps: Tip the yoghurt into a sieve lined with a clean tea towel, set over a bowl. Leave 30 minutes to drain. Warm the milk, stir in the saffron and let it steep.
Put the caster sugar, water and lemon juice in a wide pan. Lightly crush 6 cardamom pods and add them. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Peel, quarter and core the pears. Slip them into the syrup and poach gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Lift out and set aside.
Boil the syrup hard for 5 minutes until glossy and slightly thick. Toast the pistachios in a dry pan for 3 minutes, then chop roughly.
Split the last 2 pods, crush the seeds to a powder and beat into the drained yoghurt with the icing sugar and saffron milk. Chill until needed.
Spoon the shrikhand into bowls, top with warm pears, a drizzle of syrup (pods removed) and the pistachios.
image_prompt: A shallow ceramic bowl of pale golden saffron-yellow yoghurt cream, topped with glossy amber poached pear quarters, a drizzle of syrup and scattered chopped green pistachios, with a few whole cardamom pods and saffron threads beside it.
alt_text: Bowl of golden saffron yoghurt topped with glossy poached pear quarters, syrup and chopped green pistachios, with cardamom pods alongside.
caption_hook: Shrikhand is the pudding I'd happily eat at every Diwali table. This one gets pears, because it's autumn and they deserve a party too. Anyone else a saffron hoarder?
